body:
@Mrodent thank you for reporting this. We didn't make any intentional changes to the `fvh` highlighter behavior between 7.10 and 7.16. I was able to reproduce using the mappings you sent and confirmed it's a regression.

I think this is caused by https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/74348, where we no longer extract sub-paths in `SourceLookup#extractRawValues`. The `fvh` highlighter still uses this code path, which means it misses highlights on multi-fields. We will look into fixing this in an upcoming Elasticsearch version.
@romseygeek would you be up for looking at this since you're very familiar with #74348 and the highlighting code?

Thanks for the confirm. Will keep an eye-out for progress.

Incidentally, as as side-note for @romseygeek: 

If I change from "simple_query_string" to "query_string" (and this applies even in 7.10.2), I find that the colouring (i.e. the order in which the `pre-tag`s are applied) seems to become haphazard. I.e. instead of term 1: yellow, term 2: skyblue, term 3: lightgreen, I might find the results highlighted: 1: lightcoral, 2: silver, 3: lightcoral (again). 

This is clearly not my intention: I want the highlighting colours (i.e. tags) to apply in the order given.

Knowing less than nothing about what's going on under the hood here, I have no knowledge whether this can be addressed at the same time. But it'd be nice.

I expect them to be highlighted as in the previous version of ES. **Steps to reproduce**: Index mappings with a field and subfield with identical analysis, both have term vectors with positions offsets. ``` PUT /test { "mappings": { "properties": { "query": { "type": "percolator" }, "userinput": { "type": "text", "analyzer": "standard", "term_vector": "with_positions_offsets", "fields": { "another": { "type": "text", "analyzer": "standard", "term_vector": "with_positions_offsets" } } } } } } ``` A couple of test documents: ``` PUT /test/_doc/1?refresh=true { "query": { "match_phrase": { "userinput": { "query": "kimchi" } } } } PUT /test/_doc/2?refresh=true { "query": { "match_phrase": { "userinput.another": { "query": "kimchi" } } } } ``` The actual search query: ``` GET /test/_search { "query": { "percolate": { "field": "query", "document": { "userinput": "kimchi" } } }, "highlight": { "type": "fvh", "fields": { "*": {} } } } ``` This sequence would respond with the following on 7.16.2, notice that the second document contains no highlighting. ```json { "took": 3, "timed_out": false, "_shards": { "total": 1, "successful": 1, "skipped": 0, "failed": 0 }, "hits": { 0.13076457, "_source": { "query": { "match_phrase": { "userinput.another": { "query": "kimchi" } } } }, "fields": { "_percolator_document_slot": [0] } } ] } } ``` Executing the same sequence on 7.9.3 highlights both of the results: ```json { "took": 2, "timed_out": false, "_shards": { "total": 1, "successful": 1, "skipped": 0, "failed": 0 }, "hits": { "total": { "value": 2, "relation": "eq" }, "max_score": 0.13076457, "hits": [ { "_index": "test", "_type": "_doc", "_id": "1", "_score": 0.13076457, "_source": { "query": { "match_phrase": { "userinput": { "query": "kimchi" } } } }, "fields": { "_percolator_document_slot": [0] }, "highlight": { "userinput": ["kimchi"] } }, { "_index": "test", "_type": "_doc", "_id": "2", "_score": 0.13076457, "_source": { "query": { "match_phrase": { "userinput.another": { "query": "kimchi" } } } }, "fields": { "_percolator_document_slot": [0] }, "highlight": { "userinput.another": ["kimchi"] } } ] } } ``` **Provide logs (if relevant)**:

issue.title: FastVectorHighlighter should use ValueFetchers to load source data

labels.name: :Search Relevance/Highlighting
labels.description: How a query matched a document

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
FVH was relying on `SourceLookup.extractRawValues()` to load its data, but this no
longer works for multifields.  It should instead use value fetchers which will correctly
locate the input for multifields and/or copy fields.

Fixes #84690
Fixes #82458
Fixes #80895
Fixes #75011
